highlight.description: A fine light line along the inner edge, nice on dark windows.

advisories.liveUrl: The live view needs an https address, for example example.com.
advisories.url: This does not look like a web address. The bar still shows it as you typed it.

seo.whatIs: A screenshot beautifier turns a plain screen capture into a polished image. The picture sits on a background and gets padding, rounded corners, a soft shadow and, if you like, a window or browser bar with an address. Screenshots in documentation, blog posts, on social media and on Product Hunt look clean and consistent. As a website mockup it shows your page on a laptop, monitor, tablet or phone, and as a responsive mockup on several devices at once.
seo.howTo: Drop your screenshot into the editor, choose a file or paste it with Ctrl+V. Then pick a frame, padding, corners, shadow and a background: a color, a gradient or a Musterli background such as mesh, blurry or waves. Space rolls a new background and keeps your picture. Export as PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG, or copy the result straight to the clipboard. For a mockup, pick a laptop, monitor, tablet, phone or a responsive set under Device and type the address for the browser bar.

u1.title: Docs and blog posts
u1.text: Consistent padding, corners and shadows make screenshots in guides and articles look tidy. A window bar makes every picture look like part of one set.

u2.title: Product Hunt and social media
u2.text: Show your app on a gradient or Musterli background in the right sizes for Product Hunt, X or LinkedIn. The sizes are ready in the menu.

u3.title: Website mockups
u3.text: Present your site on a laptop, monitor, tablet and phone, or as a responsive set with several devices. It fits right into pitches and client decks.

tips.t1: Paste your screenshot with Ctrl+V or Cmd+V. Space rolls a new background and keeps your picture.
tips.t2: Pick a ready-made format for your platform from the size menu so nothing gets cropped.
tips.t3: Your screenshot stays in your browser. Share links leave out the picture and the address, and saved designs stay local.

faq.a1: No. The picture is processed in your browser only and never sent to a server. Share links contain neither the picture nor the address in the bar. If you save the design, everything stays local in your browser.
faq.a2: PNG, JPG, WebP and SVG up to 5 MB. Raster pictures are scaled down to at most 3840 pixels on the long side and kept as PNG so text stays sharp. SVG is cleaned of scripts and external references first.
faq.q3: Which size fits Product Hunt, X or LinkedIn?
faq.a3: The size menu has ready formats: 1270 × 760 for Product Hunt, 1600 × 900 for X and slides, 1200 × 627 for LinkedIn and 1920 × 1200 for documentation. The screenshot adapts automatically.
faq.q4: What is in the SVG export?
faq.a4: Background, shadow and window bar are vectors; your screenshot is embedded as an image (data URI). The file needs nothing else but is about as large as your picture.
faq.q5: How do I make a responsive mockup of my website?
faq.a5: Choose “Responsive set” under Device. One screenshot is enough: every device shows it, cropped to its screen from the top. You can add separate screenshots for tablet and phone. With the live view your browser loads the website right into the devices, and “Take this view” turns it into pictures. Some websites do not allow embedding; then upload a screenshot.

avatar.name: Avatar Generator
avatar.description: Profile pictures with initials, identicons or shapes, derived from a name. Circle, rounded or square, with a solid color, gradient or pattern.

name.label: Name
name.description: Gives initials, color and pattern. Same name, same avatar.

initials.label: Custom initials
initials.description: Up to three characters, replace the initials from the name.

source.label: Color and pattern from
source.description: With Random, the space bar makes a new identicon every time.

background.label: Outer background
background.description: Area outside the shape, transparent for round avatars.

seo.whatIs: An avatar generator creates profile pictures without a photo: initials on a colored shape, a symmetric identicon or a small composition of shapes. Use them as default avatars for user accounts, in comments, team pages, chats and prototypes. Color and pattern are derived from the name, so every person always looks the same.
seo.howTo: Type a name or an email address and choose initials, identicon or shapes. Set the shape, the fill (solid, gradient or pattern), the font and the grid, and pick a palette each name takes its color from. The space bar shuffles palette, fill and font while the name stays. Export as SVG, PNG, JPG or WebP, for example at 128, 256, 512 or 1024 pixels.

u1.title: Default avatars
u1.text: New accounts get a profile picture with initials or an identicon, derived from the name. The same name always gives the same picture.

u2.title: Team pages and prototypes
u2.text: Fill team pages, comment threads and chat mockups with matching avatars instead of empty circles. Drafts instantly feel more alive.

u3.title: Communities and forums
u3.text: Identicons tell accounts apart at a glance, without anyone having to upload a photo. That also protects your members' privacy.

tips.t1: Pick a palette with similar lightness, so every avatar on a page looks consistent whatever color a name gets.
tips.t2: For a fixed look, export PNG or WebP. The SVG uses system fonts and can look slightly different on other devices.
tips.t3: Export at 256 or 512 pixels. That covers high-resolution screens and keeps files small.

q1.question: Does the same name always get the same avatar?
q1.answer: Yes. Color, identicon and shapes come from a hash of the name, not from chance. Upper and lower case and surrounding spaces do not matter. Only the palette and your other settings change the result.

q2.question: Which fonts are used?
q2.answer: Only the system fonts of your device (sans, serif, mono or rounded). No font files are loaded or embedded, so the lettering can look slightly different on another operating system. For a fixed look, export PNG, JPG or WebP.

q3.question: What is an identicon?
q3.answer: An identicon is a small, symmetric pixel pattern computed from a piece of text. It tells accounts apart without anyone uploading a picture. Here you choose the grid, the cell shape and the gap.

q4.question: Is the name stored anywhere?
q4.answer: No. Everything runs in your browser. The name is only part of a share link if you create one, and of the design if you save it locally.

q5.question: Can I create many avatars at once?
q5.answer: Each export holds one avatar. Enter the names one after another: since color and pattern follow from the name, every person keeps the same look when you add more avatars later.

placeholder-image.name: Placeholder Image Generator
placeholder-image.description: Placeholder images in any size with a size label or your own text, as a solid color, gradient or pattern. For wireframes, mockups and layouts.

seo.whatIs: A placeholder image holds the space for a picture that is still missing from a layout. It shows its size in pixels or your own text, so everyone knows what goes there. You need placeholders in wireframes, mockups, prototypes, presentations and while building websites.
seo.howTo: Pick a size from the list (social media, screens, ad formats) or enter width and height. The label shows width × height automatically, your own text or nothing. Then choose a solid color, a gradient or a pattern and turn on diagonals or a border. Export as SVG, PNG, JPG or WebP.

u1.title: Wireframes and mockups
u1.text: Placeholders with a size label show the whole team which picture goes where. No image format gets lost in the handoff.

u2.title: Building websites
u2.text: Download the images as files instead of relying on someone else's placeholder service. Nothing breaks when a service goes down.

u3.title: Ad formats
u3.text: Test layouts for banners such as 300 × 250 or 728 × 90 with placeholders at the right size. The formats are ready in the size list.

tips.t1: Use your own text instead of the size label to describe the content, such as Team photo or Product shot. It makes handoffs easier.
tips.t2: Diagonals and a border make placeholders instantly recognizable as such in a layout, even on white pages.
tips.t3: SVG is tiny and sharp, PNG works everywhere. Use SVG for websites and PNG for slides.

q1.question: Do I need a placeholder URL service?
q1.answer: No. You download the image as a file and add it to your project. There is no dependency on someone else's server, and nothing breaks when a service shuts down.

q2.question: Which sizes are possible?
q2.answer: Any size from 16 to 8192 pixels per side. The list has common social media formats, screens, print formats and ad banners such as 300 × 250 or 728 × 90.

q3.question: Does the text fit narrow images?
q3.answer: Yes. The label gets smaller until it fits the width. Only system fonts are used; no font files are loaded.

q4.question: Is SVG or PNG better?
q4.answer: SVG is tiny and stays sharp at any size, ideal for prototypes in code. PNG, JPG and WebP look the same everywhere, even where another system font is installed.

animated-gradient.name: Animated Gradient Generator
animated-gradient.description: Moving, rotating and color-shifting gradients and floating blobs as pure CSS. Copy CSS, Tailwind or HTML, or export PNG and GIF.

mode.label: Animation
mode.description: Pan moves a large gradient, Rotate turns it, Shift lets the colors trade places, Blobs float soft color spots.

angle.label: Angle
angle.description: Direction of the gradient. When panning, the gradient also moves along this axis.

motion.label: Motion
motion.description: How far the gradient or the blobs travel.

seo.whatIs: An animated gradient is a background that moves slowly: the gradient pans, turns, changes its colors or soft blobs drift across it. Musterli writes it as pure CSS with keyframes, without JavaScript or video, so it stays light and sharp at any size.
seo.howTo: Pick Pan, Rotate, Shift or Blobs, choose your colors and set duration, easing and direction. Press Space for new colors and a new blob layout. The preview runs the real CSS. Copy the CSS, an HTML example or Tailwind classes, export a still image as PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG, or the whole loop as a GIF.

u1.title: Hero sections
u1.text: A slowly moving gradient brings a home page to life, with no video and no JavaScript. The CSS is only a few lines long and loads instantly.

u2.title: Buttons and banners
u2.text: A subtle color shift draws the eye to calls to action, announcements or sales. The Tailwind classes make it quick to add.

u3.title: Slides and streams
u3.text: Exported as GIF, the loop runs in slides, overlays and social posts. A still frame is available as PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG too.

tips.t1: A long duration of 10 seconds or more feels calm and refined. Short loops quickly become distracting.
tips.t2: The code includes a reduced-motion rule. People who ask for less motion see the first frame as a still gradient.
tips.t3: Blobs only move with transform, which keeps the CPU load low even on older devices.

q1.question: What happens for people who prefer reduced motion?
q1.answer: Every code export includes a prefers-reduced-motion rule. People who ask their system for less motion see a calm, still gradient, exactly the first frame of the animation. The preview here behaves the same way.

q2.question: Which browsers support the rotating and color-shifting gradients?
q2.answer: They use @property, which Chrome and Edge support since version 85, Safari since 16.4 and Firefox since 128. Older browsers show a still gradient instead of a broken background.

q3.question: Does the animation slow down my page?
q3.answer: The blobs only move with transform, which the browser handles on the graphics card. Panning, rotating and shifting repaint the background, so keep them for one hero area rather than many small elements. Longer durations look calmer anyway.

q4.question: How do I use it with Tailwind?
q4.answer: The Tailwind export gives you classes with arbitrary values plus a note to add the keyframes. For Tailwind v4 there is an @theme version that defines --animate-* and the keyframes, so you can write animate-gradient-pan.

q5.question: Can I get the animation as an image?
q5.answer: PNG, JPG, WebP and SVG show the still start state. The GIF export draws the whole loop frame by frame, seamlessly, for places where CSS is not possible such as emails or chats.

favicon-generator.name: Favicon Generator
favicon-generator.description: Favicons and app icons from a letter, a shape or your logo. One click gives you a pack with every size, the manifest and the HTML.

text.label: Text
text.description: One to four characters, for example an initial.

pattern.label: Pattern
pattern.description: The pattern color sits between the base color and the foreground.

darkMode.label: Own colors in dark mode
darkMode.description: favicon.svg then switches by itself when the browser uses a dark theme.

shortName.label: Short name
shortName.description: Shown under the icon on the home screen, up to 12 characters.

splash.label: App background
splash.description: For the splash screen and behind transparent Apple and maskable icons. The theme color follows the icon background.

advisories.darkOff: The dark variant needs its own colors. Turn on own colors under Dark mode.
advisories.noLogo: Upload a logo or pick one from your Brand Kit. Until then the icon shows the text.

iconPack.label: Icon pack (ZIP)
iconPack.description: favicon.ico (16, 32, 48 px), favicon.svg, Apple touch icon, app icons at 192 and 512 px, a maskable icon, site.webmanifest and the HTML for the head.

seo.whatIs: A favicon is the small picture in the browser tab, in bookmarks and in the history. Phones show an app icon when someone adds your website to the home screen. Modern websites need several files for this: favicon.ico for older browsers, favicon.svg for every size and dark mode, an Apple touch icon, icons for Android and a manifest. The favicon generator creates all of them from one design.
seo.howTo: Choose a letter, a shape from the library or your own logo as the content. Set the background (color, gradient, pattern or transparent), the tile shape and the padding. Press Space for new colors. Turn on own colors for dark mode if you like and enter the name and colors under App and manifest. Then export the icon pack as a ZIP, copy the files to the root folder of your website and paste the HTML into the head.

u1.title: A new website
u1.text: Create every file today's browsers and phones need from one letter or your logo, in a single pack. The matching HTML is included.

u2.title: Web apps
u2.text: The pack includes a manifest and a maskable icon, so your app looks clean on the Android home screen whatever shape the system cuts out.

u3.title: Side projects and docs
u3.text: A simple favicon with an initial makes even small projects easy to spot among browser tabs. It takes just a few minutes.

tips.t1: Think of the smallest size, 16 pixels in a browser tab. Fine details disappear there, a bold letter or a simple shape stays recognizable.
tips.t2: Own colors in dark mode let favicon.svg adapt to dark browser bars.
tips.t3: Your logo from the Brand Kit is ready in the Logo field. Then copy the files to your root folder and the HTML into the head.

q1.question: Which files are in the icon pack?
q1.answer: favicon.ico with 16, 32 and 48 px, favicon.svg, apple-touch-icon.png (180 px), icon-192.png, icon-512.png, icon-512-maskable.png for Android, site.webmanifest and head-snippet.html with the matching tags. These are the files current browsers and phones actually use.

q2.question: What is a maskable icon?
q2.answer: Android cuts app icons into circles, drops or rounded squares. A maskable icon therefore fills the whole area and keeps its content in the safe zone, a circle with 80 % diameter. The Maskable variant shows you how it looks.

q3.question: How does the favicon work in dark mode?
q3.answer: With own colors in dark mode, favicon.svg holds both variants and the browser picks one through prefers-color-scheme. The HTML gets a second theme-color for dark interfaces as well.

q4.question: Is my logo uploaded?
q4.answer: No. Everything happens in your browser, including packing the ZIP. Your logo is not part of the share link, and SVG files are cleaned of scripts and external references first.

q5.question: Why does the letter look slightly different on another device?
q5.answer: Text uses the device's system fonts, so no font files are needed. The PNG files are drawn with the fonts of your computer. For an identical result everywhere, use a shape or your logo as SVG.

duotone.name: Duotone and Gradient Map
duotone.description: Tint photos in two, three or more colors: duotone, tritone and gradient map with a tone curve and grain. Your picture stays on your device.

photo.label: Your photo
photo.description: PNG, JPG or WebP up to 5 MB. Drop the picture here, choose a file or paste it with Ctrl+V (Mac: Cmd+V). It stays in your browser; share links leave it out. Without a photo Musterli shows a sample picture.

seo.whatIs: Duotone is an image effect that reduces a photo to two colors: dark areas take the shadow color, light areas the highlight color, with a smooth blend in between. With three colors it is called tritone, with any number a gradient map. The look is popular for posters, album covers, social media and websites because it tints photos in brand colors.
seo.howTo: Upload a photo or try the presets on the sample picture. Choose duotone, tritone or gradient and set the shadow and highlight colors. Brightness, contrast and gamma decide how much area each color gets. Grain adds an analog print look, strength blends the original back in. Space rolls new color pairs. Export as PNG, JPG or WebP at full resolution.

u1.title: Photos in brand colors
u1.text: Tint team and product photos consistently, so pictures from different sources belong together and look like a planned series.

u2.title: Posters and album covers
u2.text: Bold color pairs such as pink and blue give photos a graphic, poster-like look. It works with simple phone photos too.

u3.title: Websites and social media
u3.text: Duotone images as backgrounds keep text readable and still stand out. Light highlight colors make the picture calmer.

tips.t1: Gamma shifts how much area the shadow and highlight colors get, often to better effect than brightness alone.
tips.t2: A brand palette from your Brand Kit is sorted by lightness: the darkest color becomes the shadow, the lightest the highlight.
tips.t3: A little grain adds an analog print look. Strength blends the original back in.

faq.a1: No. The photo is processed in your browser only and never sent to a server. Share links leave the photo out; if you save the design, everything stays local in your browser.
faq.q2: How large can the photo be?
faq.a2: Files up to 5 MB as PNG, JPG or WebP. Photos up to 4096 pixels on the long side keep their full resolution, 12 megapixel pictures included. The design size follows the photo, and the export computes the effect at that size.
faq.q3: What is the difference between duotone, tritone and gradient map?
faq.a3: Duotone gives every brightness a color between two colors, tritone adds a color for the midtones. A gradient map takes any number of colors, spread evenly from dark to light. Colors are blended in the OKLab color space, so the transitions stay clean.
faq.q4: Can I use my brand colors?
faq.a4: Yes. Apply a brand palette from your Brand Kit: Musterli sorts the colors by lightness, the darkest becomes the shadow color and the lightest the highlight color.
faq.q5: Why is there no SVG export?
faq.a5: The effect changes every pixel of the photo, so the result is a raster image. An SVG with a filter would look different from app to app. PNG, JPG and WebP show exactly what you see in the preview.

ascii-art.name: ASCII Art
ascii-art.description: Turn photos into ASCII art from characters, colored characters, an LED dot matrix or braille. Export as SVG, PNG, text or HTML.

photo.label: Your photo
photo.description: PNG, JPG or WebP up to 5 MB. Drop the picture here, choose a file or paste it with Ctrl+V (Mac: Cmd+V). It stays in your browser; share links leave it out. Without a photo Musterli shows a sample picture.

customRamp.label: Custom characters
customRamp.description: From light to dark, at most 64 characters. The first one stands for the lightest areas, usually a space.

seo.whatIs: ASCII art is a picture made of text characters: dark areas get dense characters such as @ or #, light areas dots or spaces. From a little distance the photo appears again. Musterli also draws colored characters, an LED or dot matrix and braille patterns, for posters, terminal aesthetics, README files and websites.
seo.howTo: Upload a photo or start with the sample picture. Choose characters, dots or braille, the number of columns and a character set, including your own characters. Brightness, contrast and gamma decide how much detail shows; invert fits the picture to a dark background. Export as SVG, PNG, JPG or WebP, or as text and an HTML snippet.

u1.title: READMEs and terminals
u1.text: A logo or portrait made of text fits README files, command-line tools and startup banners. The text export pastes right in.

u2.title: Posters and merch
u2.text: Colored ASCII art or an LED dot matrix makes posters, T-shirts and covers with retro charm. As SVG it stays sharp at any size.

u3.title: Websites
u3.text: The HTML snippet puts the characters on your page as real text, light and copyable. It suits portfolios and sites with a terminal look.

tips.t1: More columns show finer detail but smaller characters. For text in READMEs, 60 to 100 columns read well.
tips.t2: For dark backgrounds, turn on Invert so light areas become dense characters.
tips.t3: Contrast and gamma decide how much of the picture stays recognizable. Portraits on a calm background work best.

faq.a1: No. The photo is processed in your browser only and never sent to a server. Share links contain neither the photo nor the characters computed from it; a shared link shows the sample picture.
faq.a2: Your system's monospace font, for example SF Mono, Menlo, Consolas or Liberation Mono. Musterli loads no web font. In the SVG every row is exactly as wide as the picture, so the art fits with another font too.
faq.q3: How large do SVG and text get?
faq.a3: At most 32,000 cells, or 32,000 dots for braille. More columns show finer detail; beyond that Musterli shrinks the grid evenly. That keeps an SVG under 1 MB, even in color.
faq.q4: What is the difference between size and lit dots?
faq.a4: With size, dots grow with darkness like in halftone print. With lit, all dots are the same size and their opacity follows the brightness, like an LED display. Invert makes the light areas glow.
faq.q5: Can I use the ASCII art as text?
faq.a5: Yes. The export offers plain text for README files, code comments and terminals, plus an HTML snippet with inline styles that brings its colors and the monospace font along.

perspective-grid.name: 3D Perspective Grid
perspective-grid.description: Retro grid in 3D perspective with sun, stars, mountains and glow, the synthwave and outrun look. Export as SVG, image or animated GIF.

cameraHeight.label: Camera height
cameraHeight.description: Height above the floor in grid cells. Close to the floor the cells look large and flat, from high up you see many small cells. This is also the line spacing.

seo.whatIs: A perspective grid is a floor grid that runs into the distance and vanishes at the horizon, familiar from synthwave, outrun and eighties video games. Musterli computes the grid with a real camera projection and can add a striped sun, stars, mountains, haze and glow. Use it as a background for album covers, streams, slides or websites.
seo.howTo: Pick a preset or set horizon, tilt, field of view and camera height yourself. Under Grid you adjust view distance, line width, fade and glow, under Scene the sun, stars, mountains and haze. Press the space bar for new colors and a new camera. Export as SVG, PNG, JPG or WebP, or as a GIF in which the grid moves forward in a seamless loop.

u1.title: Album covers and music
u1.text: A glowing grid with a striped sun is the synthwave and outrun look for covers, playlists and flyers. Neon colors on a dark base work best.

u2.title: Streams and gaming
u2.text: Behind overlays, start screens and tournament graphics, it brings back the look of eighties video games. As a GIF the grid moves in a loop.

u3.title: Events and slides
u3.text: A perspective grid on the title slide gives retro parties and tech talks an instant style. The SVG stays editable in Figma or Illustrator.

tips.t1: A low horizon leaves room in the sky for the sun and mountains, a high one puts the grid up front.
tips.t2: Glow and horizon haze soften the image. For a crisp vector look, turn both off.
tips.t3: In the GIF the grid moves exactly one cell per loop, so the animation runs seamlessly.

q1.question: Do I need 3D software for this?
q1.answer: No. Musterli computes the perspective right in your browser and draws every line as a vector. The SVG stays sharp at any size and opens in Figma, Illustrator or Inkscape.

q2.question: How is the animation made?
q2.answer: Choose GIF in the export and the Motion source. The grid moves exactly one cell depth towards you per loop, so the loop is seamless. The first frame matches the preview.

q3.question: Why does the grid end before the horizon?
q3.answer: Far away the lines lie so close together that only flicker remains. Musterli fades the grid out before that and fills the rest with haze. View distance and fade decide how far it reaches.

q4.question: Can I use my brand colors?
q4.answer: Yes. With a brand palette from your Brand Kit the tool uses your colors for the sky, lines, sun, stars and mountains. The floor color stays so the contrast works.

halftone.name: Halftone Effect
halftone.description: Turn photos into halftone dots, lines, squares or diamonds like newspaper print. With screen angle, cell size, two colors and SVG export. Your picture stays on your device.

photo.label: Your photo
photo.description: PNG, JPG or WebP up to 5 MB. Drop the picture here, choose a file or paste it with Ctrl+V (Mac: Cmd+V). It stays in your browser; share links leave it out. Without a photo Musterli shows a sample picture.

seo.whatIs: Halftone is the technique newspapers and posters use to print photos with a single ink: the picture is split into a grid of cells, and each cell gets a dot that grows the darker the picture is at that spot. Up close you see dots, from a distance a photo. Today the look is popular for posters, merch, social media and websites with a retro or pop art style.
seo.howTo: Upload a photo or try the presets on the sample picture. Choose the shape (dots, lines, squares or diamonds), the cell size and the screen angle. Ink and paper are up to you, and the paper can be transparent. Invert turns the light areas into dots, ideal for light ink on a dark background. Brightness, contrast and gamma decide how large the dots get. Space rolls new colors and angles. Export as PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG.

u1.title: Posters and merch
u1.text: Halftone dots give photos a pop art or newspaper look for posters, T-shirts and tote bags. With a single ink it looks especially graphic.

u2.title: Screen printing and plotters
u2.text: The SVG export draws every dot as a vector, ready for screen printing, lasers or cutting plotters. No image editor needed.

u3.title: Websites and social media
u3.text: A single-ink halftone in your brand color on transparent paper looks graphic and loads fast. It sits on any background of your site.

tips.t1: 45 degrees is the classic screen angle, where the eye notices the grid least. 0 degrees looks technical and strict.
tips.t2: For light ink on a dark background, turn on Invert. The light areas of the photo then become dots.
tips.t3: Larger cells look bolder and keep the SVG small. Very large photos need a larger cell size for the SVG.

faq.a1: No. The photo is processed in your browser only and never sent to a server. Share links leave the photo out; if you save the design, everything stays local in your browser.
faq.q2: Can I export the halftone as a vector?
faq.a2: Yes. The SVG export draws every dot and line as a vector shape, ideal for plotters, screen printing or lasers. To keep the file manageable (about 1 MB), it is limited to 70,000 shapes. For very large photos, choose a larger cell size; PNG, JPG and WebP have no such limit.
faq.q3: Which screen angle is right?
faq.a3: 45 degrees is the classic: at this angle the eye notices the grid least. 0 degrees looks technical and strict, lines at 30 degrees recall copper engravings. Press space to try different angles.
faq.q4: Why do the dots turn into a flat area in a small preview?
faq.a4: When the cells are smaller than about four screen pixels in the preview, the dots cannot be shown. The preview then shows the tone the screen gives from a distance. Zoom to 100 percent to see the dots; the export always renders at full size.
faq.q5: Can I use my brand colors?
faq.a5: Yes. Apply a brand palette from your Brand Kit: the darkest color becomes the ink, the lightest the paper. With invert on, it is the other way round.

cmyk-halftone.name: CMYK Halftone
cmyk-halftone.description: Separate photos into cyan, magenta, yellow and black with a screen angle per ink, like offset printing. With misregistration and SVG export. Your picture stays on your device.

photo.label: Your photo
photo.description: PNG, JPG or WebP up to 5 MB. Drop the picture here, choose a file or paste it with Ctrl+V (Mac: Cmd+V). It stays in your browser; share links leave it out. Without a photo Musterli shows a sample picture.

seo.whatIs: CMYK halftone printing is the process behind almost every printed color photo: the picture is separated into the four process inks cyan, magenta, yellow and black, and each ink is printed as its own dot screen. So the screens do not interfere into distracting patterns (moiré), each ink has its own angle, classically cyan 15, magenta 75, yellow 0 and black 45 degrees. Up close you see the typical rosettes that comics and pop art made famous.
seo.howTo: Upload a photo or start with a preset on the sample picture. Set the cell size and shape; gray component replacement (GCR) decides how much of the gray prints in black instead of the three colored inks. The angle of each ink is adjustable. Misregistration shifts cyan, magenta and yellow against each other like a slipped print. Inks and paper can be changed. Space turns all screens together and picks a new paper. Export as PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG.

u1.title: Pop art and comics
u1.text: The typical rosettes of four-color printing give photos the look of vintage comics and posters. Up close you see dots, from a distance the picture.

u2.title: Posters and record covers
u2.text: Misregistration makes the picture look like a slightly slipped print, popular for music and culture posters. You set the direction of the shift yourself.

u3.title: Riso look
u3.text: With your own inks instead of CMYK you get a risograph-style look, ideal for zines and flyers. The paper takes any color you like too.

tips.t1: The classic angles of 15, 75, 0 and 45 degrees avoid moiré. If you change them, watch out for distracting patterns.
tips.t2: Gray component replacement (GCR) sets how much gray prints in black instead of three inks. More GCR looks cleaner.
tips.t3: This is a design effect, not a color separation for the print shop. For true-to-original photos, the printer needs a color profile.

faq.a1: No. The photo is processed in your browser only and never sent to a server. Share links leave the photo out; if you save the design, everything stays local in your browser.
faq.q2: Is this a real color separation for the print shop?
faq.a2: No, it is a design effect. The conversion from RGB to CMYK is deliberately simple and uses no color profile. To print a photo in its original colors, the print shop still needs a profile such as ISO Coated. The result works well as artwork that looks like halftone print.
faq.q3: What does gray component replacement (GCR) do?
faq.a3: Where cyan, magenta and yellow together make a gray, GCR replaces that share with black. At 100 percent a neutral gray prints in black only, at 0 percent in the three colored inks only. Values in between give rich shadows with colored rosettes.
faq.q4: Can I edit the SVG further?
faq.a4: Yes. Each ink is its own group with the multiply blend mode, so browsers and Figma show the same overprints as the preview. Apps without blend modes show the inks stacked. The SVG is limited to 70,000 shapes (about 1 MB); for large photos, choose a larger cell size.
faq.q5: Why do I see moiré patterns?
faq.a5: Moiré appears when screens with similar angles overlap, or when the cells are only a few pixels wide in the preview. The classic angles are 30 degrees apart and keep moiré small. Zoom to 100 percent or choose a larger cell size.

dither.name: Dither Effect
dither.description: Reduce photos to a few colors with Floyd-Steinberg, Atkinson, Stucki or Bayer dithering, in 1-bit, grayscale, retro palettes or your own colors. Your picture stays on your device.

photo.label: Your photo
photo.description: PNG, JPG or WebP up to 5 MB. Drop the picture here, choose a file or paste it with Ctrl+V (Mac: Cmd+V). It stays in your browser; share links leave it out. Without a photo Musterli shows a sample picture.

seo.whatIs: Dithering lets a picture get by with only a few colors and still show gradients and detail: instead of rounding a color, the algorithm spreads the difference to the neighboring pixels (error diffusion such as Floyd-Steinberg, Atkinson or Stucki) or compares each pixel with a fixed threshold pattern (Bayer matrix). The grainy look recalls early computers, game consoles and fax machines and is popular today for retro graphics, posters and websites.
seo.howTo: Upload a photo or try the presets on the sample picture. Choose an algorithm and a palette: 1-bit with two colors of your choice, four grays, four greens, the four colors of early PC graphics or your own colors. Pixel size makes the dots coarser; brightness, contrast and gamma decide how much turns light or dark. Space rolls new colors, or a new algorithm for fixed palettes. Export as PNG, JPG or WebP.

u1.title: Retro and pixel graphics
u1.text: Dithering in a few colors recalls early computers and game consoles. It suits games, retro websites and pixel art projects.

u2.title: Posters and zines
u2.text: A 1-bit picture in two bold colors prints cleanly and looks graphic. It stays clear even on simple printers and copiers.

u3.title: Light images for websites
u3.text: Few colors mean small PNG files with a character of their own. That saves load time and gives your site a distinctive look.

tips.t1: Floyd-Steinberg gives fine, natural transitions. Atkinson makes highlights and shadows bolder, Bayer a regular crosshatch.
tips.t2: Larger pixels keep the effect visible on high-resolution screens. For pixel art, 3 to 6 pixels work well.
tips.t3: Choose Custom colors under Palette and apply a brand palette from your Brand Kit for dithering in your brand colors.

faq.a1: No. The photo is processed in your browser only and never sent to a server. Share links leave the photo out; if you save the design, everything stays local in your browser.
faq.a2: Floyd-Steinberg is the classic with fine, natural transitions. Atkinson passes on only part of the error: highlights and shadows get bolder, like early Macintosh graphics. Stucki spreads the error further and looks calmer. The Bayer patterns create a regular crosshatch that suits pixel art.
faq.q3: Does the export look exactly like the preview?
faq.a3: Yes. The dithering is always computed on the same grid, the design size divided by the pixel size, and then scaled to the screen or export size. At the same size, preview and PNG are identical pixel for pixel; at twice the size every dot simply gets larger. In a reduced preview the dots blend into grays; zoom to 100 percent to see them.
faq.q4: Can I use my brand colors?
faq.a4: Yes. Apply a brand palette from your Brand Kit: the palette switches to custom colors with your brand colors, sorted from dark to light. By color picks the closest color for each pixel, by brightness spreads the photo's brightness over the palette.
faq.q5: Why is there no SVG export?
faq.a5: In dithering every pixel is a dot of its own. As SVG it would turn into hundreds of thousands of rectangles, a large and slow file. Export as PNG: with a pixel size above 1, every dot stays sharp when enlarged.

shader-gradient.name: Shader Gradient
shader-gradient.description: Liquid, silky and grainy gradients from a GPU shader. With domain warping, Bayer dithering, grain and vignette. PNG, JPG and WebP up to 8K, plus seamless GIF loops.

time.label: Moment
time.description: Position in the loop. Every export shows exactly this moment, and the GIF loop starts here.

speed.label: Speed
speed.description: How fast the preview moves. 0 stops it. With reduced motion turned on in your system, the preview always stands still.

seo.whatIs: A shader gradient is a gradient computed by a small program right on your graphics card. Instead of a few fixed color stops, it builds a living field of noise, bends it with domain warping and then runs it through your colors. The result is liquid, silky or grainy backgrounds that need no image as a starting point. Musterli renders everything in your browser, nothing leaves your device.
seo.howTo: Pick a style such as Liquid, Silk or Aurora and choose two to six colors. Shape the field with frequency, warp and angle, then give it a surface with grain, vignette and Bayer dithering. Press Space for new colors and a new shape. The moment slider picks the still frame for exports. Then export a PNG, JPG or WebP up to 8K, or a seamless GIF loop.

u1.title: Hero sections and apps
u1.text: Liquid, silky gradients make an eye-catching background for product and AI websites. Every variation is unique and needs no photo to start from.

u2.title: Wallpapers up to 8K
u2.text: Export PNG, JPG or WebP up to 8K for desktops, TVs and large displays. Grain and dithering stay exactly as in the preview.

u3.title: Animated loops
u3.text: As a seamless GIF, the gradient loops in slides, social posts and streams. Speed decides how calm the motion feels.

tips.t1: The Moment slider picks the still frame that gets exported, so you can catch the best point of the motion.
tips.t2: Dithering and grain prevent banding in soft gradients, especially in JPG and WebP.
tips.t3: Apply a brand palette from your Brand Kit and the shader runs through your brand colors. Space then only changes the shape.

q1.question: Do I need a special graphics card?
q1.answer: No. Any current browser with WebGL2 will do, and Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari have supported it for years. If WebGL2 is missing, for example because hardware acceleration is turned off, Musterli shows a notice instead of an empty area.

q2.question: Does the export look exactly like the preview?
q2.answer: Yes. Preview and export run the same shader with the same values. Musterli renders large exports up to 8K in tiles, and grain and dithering stay exactly where they are in the preview.

q3.question: What does Bayer dithering do?
q3.answer: It reduces the gradient to a few color steps and spreads the transitions in a regular dot pattern. That gives a retro look like old computers and printers, and it prevents visible banding in soft gradients.

q4.question: Can I use the gradient as an animation?
q4.answer: The GIF export draws a seamless loop whose first frame is exactly your still image. The preview moves at the speed you set, unless you have turned on reduced motion in your system.

q5.question: Does the same gradient always look the same?
q5.answer: Yes. The noise depends only on the seed and your settings. A share link or a saved design gives the same picture on every device.

god-rays.name: God Rays Effect
god-rays.description: Let light pour through your photo: rays from a light source you place, with strength, length, decay and color. Your picture stays on your device.

photo.label: Your photo
photo.description: PNG, JPG or WebP up to 5 MB. Drop the picture here, choose a file or paste it with Ctrl+V (Mac: Cmd+V). It stays in your browser; share links leave it out. Without a photo Musterli shows a sample picture.

samples.label: Quality (samples)
samples.description: More samples give smoother rays but take longer. 64 is usually enough.

threshold.label: Threshold for bright areas
threshold.description: Only areas brighter than the threshold emit light. Lower gives more rays, higher only the brightest lights.

seo.whatIs: God rays, also called crepuscular rays or light shafts, are visible beams of light falling through gaps in clouds, trees or windows. This effect recreates them: the bright parts of your photo become the light, and every pixel gathers how much light reaches it along the line toward the light source. Dark shapes such as mountains, branches or window frames cast streaks of shadow. The result is a radial blur laid over the picture as rays.
seo.howTo: Upload a photo or try the presets on the sample picture. Place the light with Light horizontal and vertical, ideally on the sun, a lamp or a window; it may also lie outside the picture. The threshold decides which areas glow; strength, ray length and decay decide how far the rays reach. Choose a ray color and darken the picture if needed. Space rolls the light position and color. Export as PNG, JPG or WebP.

u1.title: Atmospheric cover images
u1.text: Light rays give landscape and travel photos depth and warmth. They suit blog headers, hero sections and posters.

u2.title: Stage and product
u2.text: A spotlight from above puts a product or a person in the limelight. With a darkened background it looks like a stage.

u3.title: Social media posts
u3.text: A photo with bold rays stands out in the feed. With your brand color as the light, it stays on brand.

tips.t1: Put the light right on the brightest spot, such as the sun. The rays then look natural.
tips.t2: Rays need obstacles: photos with trees, clouds, windows or mountains against a bright sky give the best streaks.
tips.t3: If the whole picture gets too bright, raise the threshold so only the brightest lights glow.

faq.a1: No. The photo is processed in your browser only and never sent to a server. Share links leave the photo out; if you save the design, everything stays local in your browser.
faq.q2: Why do I hardly see any rays?
faq.a2: Rays appear only where bright and dark areas meet. Lower the threshold so more areas glow, raise the strength or ray length, and check that the light sits on a bright spot.
faq.q3: What is the difference between Add and Screen?
faq.a3: Add adds the light to the colors, so bright areas quickly turn white, which looks bold. Screen brightens more gently and hardly blows out, good for mist and pastel tones.
faq.q4: Does the export look like the preview?
faq.a4: Yes. Preview and export run through the same computation. At the same size they are identical pixel for pixel; at other sizes the rays look the same because the light position and lengths are relative to the picture.
faq.q5: Can I use my brand color as light?
faq.a5: Yes. Apply a brand palette from your Brand Kit: the lightest color becomes the ray color. You can also pick the color yourself.

fractal-glass.name: Fractal Glass Effect
fractal-glass.description: Put your photo behind reeded glass: strips with refraction, mirroring, blur and gloss, at any width and angle. Your picture stays on your device.

photo.label: Your photo
photo.description: PNG, JPG or WebP up to 5 MB. Drop the picture here, choose a file or paste it with Ctrl+V (Mac: Cmd+V). It stays in your browser; share links leave it out. Without a photo Musterli shows a sample picture.

seo.whatIs: Fractal glass, also known as reeded or fluted glass, is a popular look in graphic design and photography: a picture appears to sit behind a pane made of many narrow glass rods. Each strip bends the light a little differently and shows a shifted, squeezed or mirrored slice, with fine gloss lines along the edges. The effect turns photos and gradients into abstract, refined backgrounds.
seo.howTo: Upload a photo or try the presets on the sample picture. Set the strip width and angle and choose a profile: flat like a prism, rounded like a glass rod, or ridged. Distortion sets how much of the picture each strip shows, Mirror flips every slice, Offset shifts the strips at random. Blur turns it into frosted glass; gloss and glass color add depth. Space rolls width, angle and distortion. Export as PNG, JPG or WebP.

u1.title: Website backgrounds
u1.text: A photo behind reeded glass becomes a calm, abstract background that keeps text readable.

u2.title: Posters and covers
u2.text: The glass look feels modern and premium. It suits album covers, posters and presentations.

u3.title: Subtly abstract images
u3.text: Reeded glass hides faces and details while the mood of the photo stays. Good for placeholders and mood images.

tips.t1: Narrow strips with high distortion give a fine, almost textile look. Wide strips show more of the subject.
tips.t2: Photos with strong colors and contrast give the best refraction, such as city lights at night or a sunset.
tips.t3: A little blur and a glass color from your Brand Kit give you a background in your brand colors.

faq.a1: No. The photo is processed in your browser only and never sent to a server. Share links leave the photo out; if you save the design, everything stays local in your browser.
faq.a2: Flat shifts and squeezes the slice evenly, like a prism. Rounded enlarges the middle of each strip and squeezes the edges, like a round glass rod. Ridged does the opposite: the edges stretch and the middle squeezes.
faq.q3: What does Offset do?
faq.a3: With an offset above 0, every strip moves by a random amount and the picture breaks into fragments. Each variant has its own pattern, and a share link shows exactly the same.
faq.q4: Does the export look like the preview?
faq.a4: Yes. Strip width and blur are given in design pixels and grow with the output. At the same size, preview and PNG are identical pixel for pixel; at twice the size everything is twice as sharp.
faq.a5: No. The effect computes every pixel from the photo, which cannot be described sensibly as vector graphics. Export as PNG, JPG or WebP, also at twice the size.

pixelate.name: Pixelate Image
pixelate.description: Turn your photo into big pixels and few colors: block size, color levels or your own palette, also as SVG. Your picture stays on your device.

photo.label: Your photo
photo.description: PNG, JPG or WebP up to 5 MB. Drop the picture here, choose a file or paste it with Ctrl+V (Mac: Cmd+V). It stays in your browser; share links leave it out. Without a photo Musterli shows a sample picture.

levels.label: Levels per channel
levels.description: How many brightness steps red, green and blue each get. 2 levels give 8 colors, 6 levels up to 216.

seo.heading: Pixelate Image (Posterize)
seo.whatIs: Pixelating merges a picture into large blocks: each block shows the mean of all the pixels it covers. Posterizing then reduces the colors, either to a few evenly spaced levels per color channel or to a fixed palette. Together they create the look of pixel art, old video games and mosaics; on its own, pixelating hides faces and details.
seo.howTo: Upload a photo or try the presets on the sample picture. Choose the pixel size: 1 keeps the resolution, larger values give coarser blocks. Under Colors, keep the original colors, reduce them to levels per channel, or give each block the closest color of your palette. Brightness, contrast and gamma adjust the tones. Space rolls colors and levels, or the pixel size for original colors. Export as PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG.

u1.title: Pixel art and games
u1.text: Big pixels in few colors recall old game consoles. Ideal for sprites, backgrounds and retro projects.

u2.title: Hide details
u2.text: Big pixels hide faces and details while colors and mood stay. The photo never leaves your browser.

u3.title: Patterns for mosaics and stitching
u3.text: The SVG export gives you every block as a vector shape, a starting point for mosaics, fuse beads or cross-stitch.

tips.t1: For pixel art, 8 to 24 pixels and 3 to 6 levels work well. More levels look more photographic.
tips.t2: Pixel size 1 with few levels gives a pure posterize effect, like a screen-printed poster.
tips.t3: Apply a brand palette from your Brand Kit: every block gets the closest brand color.

faq.a1: No. The photo is processed in your browser only and never sent to a server. Share links leave the photo out; if you save the design, everything stays local in your browser.
faq.q2: What is the difference between pixelate and posterize?
faq.a2: Pixelating lowers the resolution: each block shows the average color of its area. Posterizing lowers the number of colors without changing the resolution. Here you can use either one or both together.
faq.q3: Can I export the picture as SVG?
faq.a3: Yes. Every block becomes a rectangle, and equal neighbors in a row are merged. With very many blocks, such as pixel size 1 on a large photo, the file would be too large; the export dialog then shows the count and you export as PNG.
faq.q4: Does the export look like the preview?
faq.a4: Yes. The blocks are always computed on the same grid, the design size divided by the pixel size, and then enlarged to the screen or export size. At the same size, preview and PNG are identical pixel for pixel; at twice the size every block simply gets larger.
faq.a5: Not from the exported picture: the details are no longer in it. In Musterli your original stays as long as the design is open or saved, and you can change every setting.

svg-to-css.name: SVG to CSS
svg-to-css.title: SVG to CSS converter
svg-to-css.description: Turn SVG code into a CSS background with a compact, URL-encoded data URI.
svg-to-css.whatIs: A data URI embeds the SVG directly in your stylesheet, so the browser needs no extra request. URL encoding keeps the code shorter and more readable than Base64, which makes it the best choice for icons, patterns and backgrounds in CSS.
svg-to-css.howTo: Paste your SVG or drop an .svg file onto the field. Pick the output format, check the preview and copy the result into your CSS.

faq.q1: Why URL encoding instead of Base64?
faq.a1: SVG is text. URL encoding only escapes a few characters, so the result is usually about a third smaller than Base64 and compresses better with gzip.
faq.q2: Why does my SVG not show up?
faq.a2: An SVG used as an image needs the attribute xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" on its root element. The converter adds it if it is missing. External images and fonts inside the SVG are not loaded in CSS backgrounds.
faq.q3: Is my SVG uploaded?
faq.a3: No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser, nothing is sent to a server.

css-to-svg.name: CSS to SVG
css-to-svg.title: CSS to SVG converter
css-to-svg.description: Extract the SVG from a CSS data URI, URL-encoded or Base64, and get clean SVG code back.
css-to-svg.whatIs: Many stylesheets contain icons and patterns as embedded SVG data URIs. This converter finds the first SVG data URI in your CSS, decodes it and shows the original SVG code, so you can edit it again.
css-to-svg.howTo: Paste a CSS rule, a url() value or the bare data URI. The SVG appears next to it, ready to copy or to download as an .svg file.

faq.a1: Data URIs with the type image/svg+xml, URL-encoded or Base64, in double quotes, single quotes or without quotes.
faq.q2: My CSS contains several images. Which one do I get?
faq.a2: The first SVG data URI. To get another one, paste only the rule you need.
faq.q3: Is the SVG safe to use?
faq.a3: The preview shows the SVG as an image, so scripts in it never run here. Check SVG from unknown sources before you embed it directly in your own pages.

svg-to-base64.name: SVG to Base64
svg-to-base64.title: SVG to Base64 converter
svg-to-base64.description: Encode SVG as Base64 for data URIs, CSS, HTML or JSON.
svg-to-base64.whatIs: Base64 turns any file into plain letters and digits. For SVG it is useful wherever only Base64 is accepted, for example in some email clients, JSON APIs or older tools.
svg-to-base64.howTo: Paste your SVG or choose a file. Pick data URI, Base64 only, CSS or an HTML tag and copy the result.

faq.a1: For CSS, URL encoding is usually shorter. Base64 is about 33 percent larger than the original but works everywhere a data URI is accepted.
faq.a2: Yes. The SVG is encoded as UTF-8 before the Base64 step, so special characters survive the round trip.
faq.q3: Is there a size limit?
faq.a3: Inputs up to 5 MB are converted directly in your browser. Large data URIs slow pages down, so keep embedded graphics small.

base64-to-svg.name: Base64 to SVG
base64-to-svg.title: Base64 to SVG converter
base64-to-svg.description: Decode Base64 or a data URI back into readable SVG code.
base64-to-svg.whatIs: Embedded SVGs are hard to read as Base64. This converter decodes the string, checks that it really is an SVG and shows you the code and a preview.
base64-to-svg.howTo: Paste raw Base64, a data URI or a whole CSS line. Copy the SVG code or download it as a file.

faq.q1: Do I need the data:image/svg+xml prefix?
faq.a1: No. Raw Base64 and complete data URIs both work, line breaks and spaces are ignored.
faq.q2: Why do I get an error?
faq.a2: Either the string is not valid Base64 or the decoded content is not an SVG. For PNG, JPG and other images, use the Base64 to image converter.
faq.q3: Is my data sent anywhere?
faq.a3: No. Decoding happens locally in your browser.

image-to-base64.name: Image to Base64
image-to-base64.title: Image to Base64 converter
image-to-base64.description: Convert PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF or SVG into a Base64 data URI for CSS and HTML.
image-to-base64.whatIs: A Base64 data URI contains the whole image as text. You can paste it straight into CSS, HTML or an email template without hosting a separate file.
image-to-base64.howTo: Choose an image, drop it onto the field or paste it from the clipboard. Pick an output format and copy the result.

faq.a1: PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF and SVG up to 5 MB. The type is detected from the file content, not from the file name.
faq.a2: For small images such as icons or placeholders. Larger images are better served as separate files, because Base64 adds about 33 percent and cannot be cached on its own.
faq.q3: Is my image uploaded?
faq.a3: No. The image stays on your device, the conversion runs in your browser.

base64-to-image.name: Base64 to image
base64-to-image.title: Base64 to image converter
base64-to-image.description: Turn Base64 or a data URI back into a PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF or SVG file.
base64-to-image.whatIs: Found an image as Base64 in CSS, HTML or an API response? This converter decodes it, detects the real image type from the content and lets you save it as a file.
base64-to-image.howTo: Paste the Base64 string or data URI. Check the preview, then download the image.

faq.a1: PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF and SVG. Other content, such as HTML or scripts, is rejected.
faq.q2: The data URI says PNG, but I get a JPG. Why?
faq.a2: The converter trusts the content, not the label. If they differ, you get the file type that matches the actual data.
faq.q3: Is there a size limit?
faq.a3: Yes, decoded images can be up to 5 MB. Everything runs in your browser.

privacy.intro: Musterli is built to collect as little data as possible. There is no account, no cookies and no cross-site tracking. Motifs and images are computed in your browser. Here you can find out which data is still processed, and why.

controller.heading: Controller
paragraphs: The operator named below is responsible for processing your personal data on this website. You can reach them by email with questions about privacy and with your requests.

law.heading: Applicable law
paragraphs: This policy follows the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP). Where the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) applies, for example because you visit the website from the EU or EEA, its requirements apply as well.

Where the GDPR requires a legal basis, we process data based on our legitimate interest in running the website securely, reliably and without errors (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). If you write to us, the legal basis is answering your request (Art. 6(1)(b) or (f) GDPR).

hosting.heading: Hosting with Cloudflare
paragraphs: The website runs on Cloudflare Workers, a service of Cloudflare, Inc., 101 Townsend St., San Francisco, CA 94107, USA. Cloudflare delivers the pages through a worldwide network of data centers and protects them against attacks.

When you open a page, Cloudflare processes technically necessary data: your IP address, date and time, the requested address, the previously visited page (referrer), and your browser and operating system (user agent). This data is used for delivery, security and troubleshooting. We do not analyze it to identify you.
Data may be transferred to the USA and other countries in the process; see the section “Transfers abroad”.

analytics.heading: Statistics with Cloudflare Web Analytics
paragraphs: To understand which pages are used and how fast they load, we use Cloudflare Web Analytics. The service works without cookies and without local storage in your browser and, according to Cloudflare, creates no profiles and no fingerprint of your device.

A small script from static.cloudflareinsights.com sends the following to Cloudflare when a page is opened: the page address without query parameters, the previously visited page, browser, operating system and device type, the country (derived from the IP address), and load times and page speed metrics. We only see aggregated numbers, never individual visits.
The script only runs on the public website, not on preview or test environments.

errors.heading: Error reports with Sentry
paragraphs: To find and fix bugs, we use Sentry, a service of Functional Software, Inc., 45 Fremont Street, 8th Floor, San Francisco, CA 94105, USA. We chose the EU data region: error reports are stored in data centers in the EU (Germany).

Sentry is only loaded when an error occurs on a page. An error report contains the error message, the location in the program code, browser and operating system, the page address without query parameters and without the part after the # sign, and the time. There are no cookies, no recording of your session and no performance tracking.

Your IP address has to be processed technically for the transfer. We configured Sentry not to store IP addresses or any other personal details. Error reports are deleted automatically when the retention period of our Sentry plan ends.

cookies.heading: No cookies, only local settings
paragraphs: Musterli sets no cookies. So you don’t have to pick your theme and your preferred export format every time, your browser keeps these two settings in local storage (localStorage). They stay on your device, are not sent to us, and you can delete them at any time in your browser settings.

Designs you save, the editor’s automatic drafts and your Brand Kit (palettes, logos, shapes) are kept in your browser’s database (IndexedDB). This data also stays on your device and is not sent to us. You can delete it in Musterli itself or, like the settings, in your browser settings.

local.heading: Images stay in your browser
paragraphs: When you load an image or file into a converter or create a color palette from an image, the file is processed only in your browser. It is neither uploaded nor stored, and it is gone as soon as you close the tab.

Images you use in a tool (for example your own motif in Seamless Patterns) or add to your Brand Kit are never uploaded either. If you save the design or the Brand Kit, they stay in your browser (see above). They only leave your device when you export a file yourself, and they are never part of a share link.

liveView.heading: Live view in the Screenshot Beautifier
paragraphs: If you turn on the live view in the Screenshot Beautifier, your browser loads the website whose address you entered directly from its server, in an isolated frame. Like on any visit, that website receives technically necessary data such as your IP address, date and time and your user agent, and its own privacy policy applies. Nothing passes through Musterli, and we do not learn the address.

“Take this view” lets your browser capture a picture of this tab after you allow it. The capture stops right away and is processed only in your browser. The picture is treated like an uploaded screenshot: it stays on your device and is never part of a share link.

share.heading: Share links
paragraphs: A share link holds your motif’s settings in the part of the address after the # sign. Your browser does not send this part to our server. Anyone with the link can see the motif. Colors derived from an image are not included in the link.

contact.heading: Contact by email
paragraphs: If you write to us, we process your email address and the content of your message to answer your request. We delete the message once it is resolved and no legal retention obligation applies.

donations.heading: Donations
paragraphs: Musterli is free and funded by voluntary donations. We use Ko-fi for this, a service of Ko-fi Labs Limited, based in the United Kingdom. Musterli itself accepts no payments and receives neither payment nor account details from you.

On the home page we show a donate button from Ko-fi. For this, your browser loads a script, a stylesheet and a logo from storage.ko-fi.com when you open the home page. Ko-fi receives technically necessary data such as your IP address, date and time, the page address and your user agent. We deliberately do not load Google fonts for it. The button itself sets no cookies on Musterli and uses no local storage.

Only when you click the button does the donation form from ko-fi.com open in an embedded window. The “Support” page also links directly to Ko-fi. Ko-fi is responsible for everything that happens in the donation form or on ko-fi.com. Ko-fi and its payment providers may set cookies there, and Ko-fi’s privacy policy applies. Ko-fi may tell us the amount donated and any details you explicitly choose to share with us.
We embed the donate button because we have a legitimate interest in offering a simple way to support Musterli (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

transfer.heading: Transfers abroad
paragraphs: Cloudflare and Sentry are based in the USA. Cloudflare may also process data in other countries where it operates data centers. For the USA we rely on the providers’ certification under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework and the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, and on the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses in the providers’ data processing agreements.
We store Sentry error reports in the EU. Access from the USA, for example by the provider’s support, still cannot be ruled out.

Ko-fi is based in the United Kingdom. The European Commission and the Swiss Federal Council have recognised the United Kingdom as providing adequate data protection. Ko-fi and its payment providers may also process data in the USA.

retention.heading: Retention
paragraphs: We keep personal data only as long as needed for its purpose or required by law. We only see statistics in aggregated form. The providers delete technical logs and error reports automatically according to their retention periods.

rights.heading: Your rights
paragraphs: You have the right to access your personal data and to have incorrect data corrected. You can ask us to delete data or restrict its processing, and you can object to processing. Where applicable, you also have the right to receive your data in a common format.
To do so, write to us at the email address above. We may ask for proof of your identity.
You can also lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority: in Switzerland the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC), in the EU the authority of your country of residence.

changes.heading: Changes
paragraphs: We update this policy when the website or the services we use change. The version published on this page applies.

paragraphs: Musterli computes, exports and saves right in your browser. Saved designs, drafts and your Brand Kit live on your device only, not on our servers. Images and logos you upload never leave your device.

uploads.heading: Your content

fair.heading: Fair use
paragraphs: Use Musterli in a way that keeps it working for everyone else. In particular, automated mass requests (for example by bots or scrapers), attempts to get around security measures, and anything that disrupts operation are not allowed.
In case of misuse we may restrict or block access, also without prior notice.

u4.text: Move, scale, rotate, align, distribute and group. With guides, snapping and undo.

steps.t3: Add text, shapes, pictures or your logo and arrange them.

faq.q1: Is the social media editor free?
faq.a1: Yes. Musterli is completely free and funded by donations. There is no account, no subscription and no watermark.
faq.a2: Every layer is attached to an edge, to the centre, or stretches across. When the format changes, margins stay the same, sizes follow the short side, and text gets smaller or wraps. Nothing is cut off.
faq.q3: Where are my designs stored?
faq.a3: In your browser's storage (IndexedDB) on this device. In My designs you can export them as a file and import them again on another device.
faq.q4: Can I use my own pictures and my logo?
faq.a4: Yes. Upload pictures right in the editor; logos come from your brand kit. Both stay local and are never part of a share link.
faq.q5: Does the editor work on a phone?
faq.a5: Viewing and exporting work everywhere. For designing, a large screen is the most comfortable.
